Title: Capacity building for qualitative research in Pakistan
NewsSummary: The Social Policy Development Centre (SPDC) in collaboration with The Aga Khan University's Institute [or Educational Development (AKU-IED) is organizing an 'intensive workshop on participatory research methods.

content.text: The Social Policy Development Centre (SPDC) in collaboration with The Aga Khan University's Institute [or Educational Development (AKU-IED) is organizing an 'intensive workshop on participatory research methods titled "Qualitative Research: Life Beyond Numbers." Dr Hafiz Pasha, the Managing Director, SPDC, made the opening remarks following a welcome address by Dr Robert Baker, Director, AKU-lED. The workshop is being conducted at AKU-IED in Karimabad, Karachi, by Colin Stewart, a consultant on social policy from Ottawa, Canada. The workshop started on December 9, 1999, and will continue till May next year.

Dr Hafiz Pasha said that qualitative research in Pakistan was still underdeveloped because working with people and getting to communities was not emphasised. He urged the participants familiar with quantitative techniques to create a balance by integrating qualitative research methodologies in their work.

Dr Baker complemented SPDC on the quality and contribution of their work in Pakistan and South Asia as a whole. He hoped that participants would benefit from the interaction in the workshop and from the others at AKU-IED.

Colin Stewart, the workshop facilitator, is interested in blending both approaches for research. He said that innovations in qualitative research, of which participatory research is a part, are not coming from the West or North but from developing country experiences in Africa, Asia and generally from the South.

The first part of the workshop is being held from December 9 to 24, 1999. This will be followed by fieldwork and a final integration workshop during April-May 2000 to compile detailed research reports. Participants are from SPDC, AKU-IED and its collaborating institutions.

Established in 1993 as the University's first programme in addition to those in the health sciences, AKU-IED has gained recognition as a centre of educational excellence dedicated to the professional development of teachers and overall school improvement in Pakistan and other developing countries. AKU-IED is also committed to leading reform in education through innovation, practice, policy development and outreach.
